_readme: The ViralGadgets catalogue. tools/blocks.js renders it into every page's gadget finder (static, crawlable HTML; assets/site.js only filters). Fields: id, name, brand, type (see types), ages [kids, teens, young, adults, seniors], who [him, her] (both = anyone), price (budget | mid | premium = typical price band, never an exact price), trend [tiktok, amazon, youtube] (where it is being talked about), blurb, why (why it's trending), note (heads-up before buying), q (search words for reviews + retailers), guide (optional page slug), link (optional referral slug from shmor-site.json links), added (YYYY-MM), img ({src, alt, credit, creditUrl}: free-licence Unsplash photo; illustrative, so alt text describes the photo, not the product). Facts only: no invented prices, ratings, sales numbers or quotes.

items.name: iPhone Duo
items.blurb: Apple's first foldable iPhone: a compact phone that opens into a small tablet-sized screen.
items.why: Announced at Apple's September 2026 event, with pre-orders from 16 October and sales from 23 October in the US. Expect a wave of unboxing and durability videos.
items.note: First-generation hardware. Wait for long-term reviews of the hinge and crease, and check repair and insurance costs before buying.

img.alt: A person holding an iPhone in their hand

items.name: iPhone 18 Pro
items.blurb: Apple's latest Pro iPhone, with the A20 Pro chip and a 48MP main camera with a variable aperture.
items.why: On sale since 18 September 2026; camera comparisons against last year's model and rival Android flagships are everywhere on YouTube.
items.note: If you have an iPhone 16 Pro or 17 Pro, the upgrade is smaller than launch videos suggest. Trade-in and carrier offers often beat the sticker price.

img.alt: A smartphone with a triple camera array against a dark background

items.name: Galaxy Z Flip
items.blurb: A clamshell foldable that snaps shut to pocket size and props itself open like a mini tripod.
items.why: Creators love the half-folded hands-free mode for selfies and video, and the cover screen for framing shots with the main camera.
items.note: Folding screens are softer than normal glass. A good case and screen cover plan are worth it.

img.alt: A man holding a smartphone in his hands

items.name: Apple Watch Series 12
items.blurb: Apple's mainstream smartwatch, adding a daily readiness score to its health and fitness tracking.
items.why: Launched September 2026. Health features such as fall detection and emergency SOS also make Apple Watch a popular gift for older relatives.
items.note: Only works with an iPhone. Older models often go on sale when a new one launches, and cover most of the same features.

img.alt: Space grey Apple Watch with a black sports band

items.name: Oura Ring
items.blurb: A smart ring that tracks sleep, activity and recovery without a screen on your wrist.
items.why: Smart rings are one of the fastest-growing wearable categories, and sleep-score screenshots are a staple of wellness TikTok.
items.note: Most features need a paid Oura membership. Use the free sizing kit before ordering.

img.alt: A rumpled bed with striped bedding in soft morning light

items.name: Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses
items.blurb: Sunglasses with a built-in camera, open-ear speakers and Meta AI voice assistant.
items.why: Hands-free point-of-view video has become its own genre on TikTok and Reels.
items.note: A light shows when you're recording, but always respect people's privacy. The Meta Ray-Ban Display version (with a screen in the lens) has had limited availability outside the US.

img.alt: Black wayfarer-style sunglasses

items.name: Bounce kids' smartwatch
items.blurb: An LTE smartwatch for children: calls and messages with approved contacts, plus location sharing, without a smartphone.
items.why: A popular "first phone" alternative as more parents delay giving children a smartphone.
items.note: Needs a monthly data subscription. Check it is sold and supported in your country before buying.

img.alt: A smartwatch with a colourful app display

items.name: AirPods 5
items.blurb: Apple's new standard AirPods, now with active noise cancellation as standard.
items.why: Launched September 2026. AirPods are perennial Amazon best-sellers and one of the most-wanted gifts for teens.
items.note: There are two versions: one with a wireless charging case and touch volume control, one without. Check which you're buying.

img.alt: White wireless earbuds charging case

items.name: WH-1000XM6
items.blurb: Sony's flagship noise-cancelling over-ear headphones, a long-running favourite for flights and commutes.
items.why: A fixture in "best headphones" round-ups, regularly compared with Bose and Apple's AirPods Max by YouTube reviewers.
items.note: The previous model (XM5) is often heavily discounted and still excellent.

img.alt: Black wireless headphones on a white table

items.name: QuietComfort Ultra Headphones
items.blurb: Bose's top noise-cancelling headphones, known for comfort on long trips.
items.why: The main rival to Sony in every noise-cancelling showdown video.
items.note: Try both brands on if you can: fit and comfort matter more than spec sheets.

img.alt: Flat lay of wireless over-ear headphones

items.name: Flip portable speaker
items.blurb: A rugged, water-resistant Bluetooth speaker for the beach, the park or the bathroom.
items.why: A constant Amazon best-seller in portable speakers, and a go-to for "waterproof speaker test" videos.
items.note: Older Flip models drop in price when a new one launches and sound almost the same.

img.alt: A black portable speaker on a wooden table

items.name: OpenRun open-ear headphones
items.blurb: Bone-conduction headphones that sit in front of your ears, so you can still hear traffic.
items.why: Popular with runners and cyclists, and part of a wider open-ear audio trend.
items.note: Bass and noise isolation are weaker than in-ear buds by design.

img.alt: Black and white headphones on a white table

items.name: Nothing Ear
items.blurb: Earbuds with a see-through design that stand out from the white-bud crowd.
items.why: Nothing's transparent look gets a lot of attention from tech creators and design fans.
items.note: Check app features on your phone: some extras work best with Nothing's own phones.

img.alt: Black and blue wireless earbuds

items.name: Volume-limited kids' headphones
items.blurb: Small, bendy headphones that cap the volume for younger ears.
items.why: Steady Amazon best-sellers for tablets, car journeys and flights.
items.note: Look for a clear volume limit (often 85 dB) and a cable-free option if your child's tablet has no headphone jack.

img.alt: A person wearing headphones

items.name: Charmera keychain camera
items.blurb: A tiny working digital camera on a keyring, sold in blind boxes so you don't know which colour you'll get.
items.why: Sold out within a day at launch in 2025, and restocks have kept selling out. Grainy, retro photos are the point.
items.note: 1.6MP: a fun toy, not a phone replacement. Rare editions resell for far more than the retail price, so beware of scalpers.

img.alt: A small white and black point-and-shoot camera

items.name: Instax Mini instant camera
items.blurb: Point, shoot and get a credit-card-sized print in seconds.
items.why: One of the most-gifted cameras on Amazon, and a staple of scrapbook and room-decor TikToks.
items.note: The film is an ongoing cost: factor in packs of film when you compare prices.

img.alt: A white and black instant camera on a white board

items.name: Retro compact digital cameras
items.blurb: Point-and-shoot "digicams" from the 2000s, loved for their flash-heavy, slightly blurry look.
items.why: Gen Z has made old compact cameras cool again: #digicam photo dumps are a long-running TikTok trend.
items.note: Mostly bought second-hand: check the battery, charger and memory card type are included.

img.alt: A black and silver compact camera

items.name: Osmo Pocket gimbal camera
items.blurb: A pocket-sized camera on a built-in stabiliser for smooth vlog and travel footage.
items.why: A favourite of travel vloggers who want steadier, better low-light video than a phone.
items.note: Check current availability in your country: DJI products have faced import restrictions in the US.

img.alt: A person holding a small action camera

items.name: Mini camera drones
items.blurb: Lightweight folding drones that shoot aerial photos and video, plus selfie drones that follow you.
items.why: Drone reveal shots and self-flying "follow me" selfie drones are everywhere on travel feeds.
items.note: Drone rules apply even to small drones: check the FAA (US), CAA (UK) or EASA (EU) rules before you fly, and current US availability for DJI models.

img.alt: A folding camera drone near a body of water

items.name: Insta360 X series
items.blurb: A 360° action camera: film everything around you, then pick the angle later.
items.why: The "invisible selfie stick" third-person shots are a viral effect on their own.
items.note: Editing 360 footage takes time; the phone app does most of the work.

img.alt: A compact action camera

items.name: Clip-on wireless microphones
items.blurb: Tiny clip-on mics that send clear audio straight to your phone or camera.
items.why: Those little mics you see on every talking-head TikTok: clean audio is the cheapest way to look more pro.
items.note: Check the receiver plugs into your phone (USB-C or Lightning) or connects over Bluetooth.

img.alt: A black microphone on a white surface

items.name: Bluetooth selfie stick tripod
items.blurb: A selfie stick that folds out into a tripod, with a detachable Bluetooth shutter remote.
items.why: One of the simplest, best-value creator gadgets: a constant Amazon best-seller.
items.note: Cheap clamps can be wobbly with heavy Pro and Max phones. Check the stated weight limit.

img.alt: A phone mounted on a small tripod

items.name: Nintendo Switch 2
items.blurb: Nintendo's hybrid console: play on the TV or take it with you, with a bigger screen than the original Switch.
items.why: Launched June 2025 and still one of the most-wanted gifts. Bundles and new games keep it trending.
items.note: Most original Switch games work on it, but check individual titles. Some physical games are "key cards" that download the game.

img.alt: A Nintendo Switch 2 console with a red screen

items.name: Steam Deck OLED
items.blurb: A handheld gaming PC that plays your Steam library on the go.
items.why: Still the benchmark every new PC handheld is compared to on YouTube.
items.note: Not every PC game runs well: check Valve's "Steam Deck Verified" rating for the games you care about.

img.alt: A handheld game console and controller with figurines on a desk

items.name: Meta Quest 3S
items.blurb: A standalone VR and mixed-reality headset: no PC or console needed.
items.why: The most affordable way into VR fitness, games and "VR fails" content.
items.note: Needs a Meta account; younger users need a parent-managed account. Clear a safe play space first.

img.alt: A pink and white VR headset

items.name: PlayStation Portal
items.blurb: A handheld screen with built-in DualSense controls that streams games from your PS5 or the cloud.
items.why: Lets PS5 owners play while someone else uses the TV.
items.note: It isn't a standalone console: you need a PS5 (or PlayStation Plus cloud streaming where offered) and strong Wi-Fi.

img.alt: A woman holding a video game controller

items.name: Backbone One phone controller
items.blurb: A controller that clips around your phone and turns it into a handheld console.
items.why: A popular way to play mobile, cloud and console-streamed games with proper buttons.
items.note: Buy the version that matches your phone's port (USB-C or Lightning) and check it fits with your case.

img.alt: A person playing a video game on a phone

items.name: Retro handheld consoles
items.blurb: Pocket-sized handhelds styled like classic Game Boys, for older games.
items.why: Retro handheld reviews are a booming YouTube niche, and nostalgia sells.
items.note: Only play games you own the rights to: downloading copyrighted ROMs you don't own isn't legal in most countries.

img.alt: An orange and black handheld games console

items.name: Echo Dot smart speaker
items.blurb: A small smart speaker with Alexa for music, timers, reminders and smart-home control.
items.why: One of Amazon's most heavily discounted devices in every big sale event.
items.note: It's always listening for its wake word: review the privacy settings and use the mic-off button when you want.

img.alt: A small smart speaker next to a smartphone

items.name: Echo Show smart display
items.blurb: A smart speaker with a screen: video calls, recipes, a doorbell view and a rolling photo frame.
items.why: A popular gift for grandparents: family can video call it, and photos appear on it automatically.
items.note: Set it up before gifting, and turn on the camera shutter when it's not in use.

img.alt: An older couple waving at a video call on a phone

items.name: Video doorbell
items.blurb: See and speak to whoever is at the door from your phone, wherever you are.
items.why: A top seller in every Amazon home-security sale; doorbell clips are a TikTok genre of their own.
items.note: Saving and reviewing recordings usually needs a paid plan. Point the camera at your own property, not your neighbours'.

img.alt: A black front door

items.name: LED strip & TV backlights
items.blurb: Colour-changing light strips for bedrooms, desks and behind the TV, controlled from your phone.
items.why: The backbone of every "room makeover" and gaming-setup TikTok.
items.note: Strong adhesive can peel paint off walls. Test on a hidden spot first, or use mounting clips.

img.alt: A bedroom lit with coloured LED lights

items.name: Sunset projection lamp
items.blurb: A lamp that throws a warm, golden-hour glow onto your wall.
items.why: One of the original TikTok-made-me-buy-it gadgets, and still a selfie-lighting favourite.
items.note: Very cheap versions can be flimsy. Look for a proper plug and safety marks (UL in the US, UKCA/CE in the UK/EU).

img.alt: A bedroom with warm light and a wooden bed frame

items.name: Robot vacuum & mop
items.blurb: Vacuums (and often mops) your floors on a schedule, then empties itself.
items.why: Robot vacuums are among the biggest-discount items in Black Friday and Prime sales, and pet owners love the hair-pickup videos.
items.note: Self-emptying docks need replacement bags. Check how it handles rugs, cables and pet mess.

img.alt: A black robot vacuum on a wooden floor

items.name: Digital photo frame
items.blurb: A Wi-Fi photo frame the whole family can send pictures to from their phones.
items.why: Consistently one of the most-recommended gifts for grandparents in gift guides.
items.note: Check if any features need a subscription, and pre-load photos before you wrap it.

img.alt: An older couple watching a video on a laptop

items.name: Bluetooth item trackers
items.blurb: Coin-sized trackers for keys, wallets, bags and suitcases.
items.why: "Where's my luggage?" airport videos made trackers a travel must-have.
items.note: AirTag works with iPhone and Samsung SmartTag with Galaxy phones; pick the one that matches your phone. Never use one to track a person.

img.alt: A grey hard-shell suitcase

items.name: CREAMi ice cream maker
items.blurb: Turns frozen bases into ice cream, sorbet or milkshakes in minutes.
items.why: Protein ice cream recipes made it one of TikTok's biggest kitchen gadgets.
items.note: Bases need to freeze for around a day, so it's not instant. It's loud while it spins.

img.alt: Vanilla ice cream with sprinkles

items.name: Dual-basket air fryer
items.blurb: Two independent drawers so you can cook your main and sides at once, finishing at the same time.
items.why: Air fryers are among the most-bought kitchen appliances in the US and UK, and air-fryer recipes are a TikTok staple.
items.note: Measure your worktop first: dual-basket models are wide.

img.alt: A modern white kitchen with a marble island

items.name: Ember temperature-control mug
items.blurb: A heated smart mug that keeps your coffee or tea at the temperature you choose.
items.why: A favourite desk-setup gadget and a regular in gift guides for people who "have everything".
items.note: Hand-wash only, and the battery lasts longest when it sits on its charging coaster.

img.alt: A cup of coffee next to a laptop

items.name: Portable USB blender
items.blurb: A rechargeable bottle-blender for smoothies and protein shakes on the go.
items.why: Gym-bag and smoothie-run videos keep it trending.
items.note: Small motors struggle with ice and frozen fruit chunks. Don't expect full-size blender results.

img.alt: A berry smoothie in a glass jar

items.name: Airwrap multi-styler
items.blurb: A hair styler that uses airflow to curl, wave and smooth hair with less extreme heat.
items.why: One of TikTok's most-reviewed beauty gadgets, with endless "Airwrap vs dupe" comparisons (Shark FlexStyle is the best-known rival).
items.note: Buy from Dyson or an authorised retailer: fake Airwraps are a known scam on social ads and marketplaces.

img.alt: Styling long blonde hair with a round brush

items.name: LED light therapy face mask
items.blurb: A wearable mask with red (and sometimes near-infrared) LEDs, used at home as part of a skincare routine.
items.why: The glowing-mask selfie is a skincare TikTok icon.
items.note: Results vary and need regular use over weeks. If you have eye conditions, take photosensitising medication or are unsure, check with a doctor or dermatologist first.

img.alt: A woman with closed eyes, photographed through glass

items.name: Mini massage gun
items.blurb: A compact percussive massager for sore muscles after the gym or a long day.
items.why: A top fitness gift, and the minis fit in a gym bag.
items.note: Avoid bones, the neck and any injury. Ask a physio if you have a medical condition.

img.alt: Close-up of a massage gun

items.name: Sunrise alarm clock
items.blurb: Wakes you with a slowly brightening light instead of a jarring beep.
items.why: A staple of "phone out of the bedroom" and better-sleep routines on TikTok.
items.note: Some models lock features behind a subscription. Check before buying.

img.alt: A black alarm clock on a white table

items.name: OneBlade hybrid trimmer
items.blurb: A trimmer and shaver in one for stubble, beards and edging.
items.why: A long-running Amazon best-seller in men's grooming.
items.note: Replacement blades are an ongoing cost: compare multi-pack prices.

img.alt: A man sitting in a barber chair

items.name: Magnetic (Qi2 / MagSafe) power bank
items.blurb: A slim battery that snaps onto the back of your phone and charges it wirelessly.
items.why: A constant TikTok and Amazon best-seller: no cables, just snap and go.
items.note: Power banks must go in your hand luggage on flights, and some airlines now restrict using them on board.

img.alt: A smartphone and a green power bank

items.name: 3-in-1 charging station
items.blurb: Charges your phone, watch and earbuds from one stand on your bedside table.
items.why: Desk-setup and nightstand videos made it a go-to tidy-up gadget.
items.note: Check it supports your watch (Apple Watch and Galaxy Watch chargers differ).

img.alt: A nightstand with a lamp, clock and chargers

items.name: Mini portable projector
items.brand: Samsung, XGIMI, Anker Nebula and others
items.blurb: A small projector for movie nights on the bedroom ceiling or the garden wall.
items.why: Ceiling-movie and backyard-cinema videos keep projectors trending, especially before the holidays.
items.note: Very cheap projectors often overstate brightness and resolution ("supports 4K" isn't native 4K). Check reviews that test in a lit room.

img.alt: A small LED projector switched on, on a table

items.name: Kindle Paperwhite
items.blurb: A waterproof e-reader with a glare-free screen and weeks of battery.
items.why: BookTok made e-readers cool again, and Kindles are among the most-discounted devices in Amazon sales.
items.note: Adjustable text size makes it a great gift for older readers. Kindle Unlimited is a separate subscription.

img.alt: An e-reader on a window sill next to a stack of books

items.name: Mechanical keyboard
items.blurb: A keyboard with individual switches for a satisfying feel and sound.
items.why: "Thocky" typing-sound ASMR is a whole genre on TikTok and YouTube.
items.note: Clicky switches are loud. Choose quieter switches if you share a room or office.

img.alt: A black and orange mechanical keyboard

items.name: MX Master mouse
items.blurb: An ergonomic wireless mouse with a fast-scrolling wheel, popular with people who work at a desk all day.
items.why: A permanent fixture in YouTubers' "what's on my desk" setup tours.
items.note: Right-handed only. Left-handers should look at symmetrical mice.

img.alt: A grey and black wireless mouse

items.name: Yoto Player
items.blurb: A screen-free audio player: children slot in cards to play stories, music and podcasts.
items.why: Parents looking to cut screen time have made screen-free audio players a gift-guide favourite (Tonies are the main rival).
items.note: Story cards are bought separately, though there is free content too.

img.alt: A young boy by a white wooden shelf

items.name: AirPods Pro 3
items.blurb: Apple’s top in-ear buds, updated in 2025 with stronger noise cancellation and heart-rate sensing for workouts.
items.why: The Pro AirPods are a staple of “what’s in my bag” videos, and the fitness features gave reviewers plenty to test.
items.note: Best with an iPhone; many features are Apple-only. The cheaper AirPods 5 now also have noise cancellation, so compare both.

img.alt: Close-up of white wireless earbuds in their case

items.name: Beats Pill
items.blurb: The revived pill-shaped Bluetooth speaker: water and dust resistant, and works with iPhone and Android.
items.why: The comeback of a 2010s icon, helped along by colourful drops and celebrity collabs.
items.note: Compare with JBL’s Flip on sound and battery before you decide; colours and prices vary by retailer.

img.alt: A black and red portable speaker

items.name: Emberton portable speaker
items.blurb: A rugged pocket speaker with Marshall’s classic guitar-amp styling.
items.why: Design-led tech is having a moment, and Marshall’s retro look photographs beautifully.
items.note: You’re partly paying for the look; check sound comparisons against cheaper rivals.

img.alt: A black and silver portable speaker

items.name: Era 100 smart speaker
items.blurb: A compact Wi-Fi speaker with stereo sound that can grow into a multi-room system.
items.why: A favourite starter speaker in home-setup and apartment-tour videos.
items.note: Sonos’s 2024 app redesign drew a lot of complaints; read recent reviews about the app before buying.

img.alt: A white and black round speaker

items.name: Bluetooth record players
items.blurb: Turntables that play vinyl and can stream to a Bluetooth speaker.
items.why: The vinyl revival is real: record collections and “Sunday spins” are all over TikTok.
items.note: Very cheap suitcase-style players can wear records faster. A basic entry-level turntable is a safer bet.

img.alt: A translucent amber vinyl record spinning on a turntable

items.name: WHOOP band
items.blurb: A screenless fitness band focused on recovery, sleep and strain.
items.why: Athletes and fitness creators made recovery scores part of their daily content.
items.note: It works on a paid membership rather than a one-off purchase. Add up the yearly cost before signing up.

img.alt: A woman running while wearing a fitness armband

items.name: Galaxy Watch
items.blurb: Samsung’s smartwatch for health tracking, workouts and notifications.
items.why: The go-to smartwatch for Android users, and a regular in every Black Friday sale.
items.note: Recent Galaxy Watches don’t work with iPhone, and some health features work best with a Samsung phone.

img.alt: A smartwatch with a black face

items.name: Budget fitness trackers
items.blurb: Slim bands that track steps, sleep and heart rate, with long battery life.
items.why: Steady Amazon best-sellers for anyone who wants the basics without a pricey smartwatch.
items.note: Accuracy varies; some brands charge for premium insights. Check the app is available in your region.

img.alt: A black fitness tracker band

items.name: X100VI
items.blurb: A premium compact camera with a fixed lens and Fujifilm’s famous film-style colour looks.
items.why: It went viral on TikTok for its “film look” straight out of the camera, and waiting lists followed.
items.note: Expensive and often hard to find; avoid inflated reseller prices and buy from authorised retailers.

img.alt: A black and grey compact camera on a wooden table

items.name: PowerShot G7 X Mark III
items.blurb: A pocket vlogging camera with a flip-up screen, loved by Gen Z for its flash-photo look.
items.why: One of the most-wanted compact cameras of the digicam revival, and frequently sold out.
items.note: It’s been on sale for years, so check you’re paying a fair price; older second-hand units are common.

img.alt: A couple of compact cameras on a table

items.name: GoPro HERO
items.blurb: The classic rugged action camera for sports, travel and point-of-view video.
items.why: Ski, surf and bike clips keep GoPros trending every season.
items.note: Cloud backup and some extras need a GoPro subscription. Factor in mounts and spare batteries.

img.alt: A black and orange action camera on a brown surface

items.name: LED ring light
items.blurb: A circular light with a phone holder for flattering, even lighting on video calls and videos.
items.why: The signature light behind countless TikTok and makeup videos.
items.note: Look for adjustable colour temperature and a sturdy stand; cheap ones can flicker on camera.

img.alt: A close-up of a ring light on a table

items.name: ROG Xbox Ally
items.blurb: A Windows gaming handheld with an Xbox-style full-screen interface, launched in October 2025.
items.why: Xbox’s first big step into handhelds made it one of the most-watched hardware launches for gamers.
items.note: There are two models at very different prices. Battery life in demanding games is short, as with most PC handhelds.

img.alt: A wireless game controller lit by cyan and magenta neon light

items.name: PlayStation 5 Pro
items.blurb: The more powerful PS5 for sharper graphics and smoother frame rates in supported games.
items.why: A favourite comparison topic on gaming YouTube: is the Pro worth it over a standard PS5?
items.note: The disc drive is sold separately. Most of the benefit shows on a 4K TV; on a 1080p screen the standard PS5 is better value.

img.alt: A white PlayStation console and controller

items.name: Wireless gaming headsets
items.blurb: Comfortable headsets with a mic for chatting with friends while gaming.
items.why: A perennial best-seller and one of the safest gifts for any gamer.
items.note: Check it supports your console (PlayStation, Xbox and Switch differ). For kids, look for volume limits.

img.alt: A person wearing orange and black headphones

items.name: Tamagotchi
items.blurb: The pocket virtual pet is back, with new models and collector editions.
items.why: 90s and Y2K nostalgia plus keyring culture made Tamagotchis a TikTok favourite again.
items.note: There are many versions with different features; check which one you’re buying, and beware of fakes on marketplaces.

img.alt: A light blue Tamagotchi virtual pet inside a green bag

items.name: Galaxy star projector
items.blurb: Projects a swirling galaxy of stars and nebula onto your ceiling.
items.why: Bedroom glow-ups and “cosy night” videos made galaxy projectors a TikTok staple.
items.note: Choose a reputable brand with clear laser-safety labelling, and don’t let young children look into the light.

img.alt: Stars in the night sky

items.name: Smart bird feeder
items.blurb: A bird feeder with a camera that snaps visiting birds and identifies them in an app.
items.why: Close-up “bird postcards” turned garden birds into a viral TikTok genre.
items.note: Some features need a subscription, and it needs decent Wi-Fi where you mount it.

img.alt: A bird perched on a bird feeder

items.name: Compact air purifier
items.blurb: A quiet HEPA purifier for bedrooms and small living spaces.
items.why: A long-running Amazon best-seller, especially during allergy and wildfire-smoke seasons.
items.note: Replacement filters are an ongoing cost. Check the clean-air delivery rate (CADR) suits your room size.

img.alt: A rectangular white device

items.name: Bambino espresso machine
items.blurb: A compact home espresso machine with a steam wand for café-style lattes.
items.why: Home coffee-bar videos made it one of the most-recommended starter espresso machines.
items.note: Sold as Breville in the US and Sage in the UK and Europe. You’ll want a decent grinder too.

img.alt: A black and silver coffee machine on a wooden table

items.name: SLUSHi frozen drink maker
items.blurb: A countertop machine that turns drinks into slushies and frozen cocktails.
items.why: One of 2025’s biggest viral kitchen launches, with endless flavour experiments on TikTok.
items.note: It’s big and takes a while to freeze each batch. Measure your counter space first.

img.alt: Slush machines with different coloured drinks

items.name: Wireless meat thermometer
items.blurb: A probe that sits in the meat and sends the temperature to your phone.
items.why: A favourite gift for barbecue fans, and a hero of “perfect steak” videos.
items.note: Bluetooth range can be limited through walls or grills; check the range of the model you choose.

img.alt: Tongs lifting a seared steak over a charcoal grill

items.name: Electric milk frother
items.blurb: A handheld or jug frother for foamy lattes, matcha and hot chocolate at home.
items.why: Iced latte and matcha routines made the humble frother a TikTok must-have.
items.note: Handheld wands are cheapest; heated jug frothers are easier for hot drinks.

img.alt: A person making latte art

items.name: High-speed hair dryer
items.blurb: A lightweight, fast-drying hair dryer with a high-speed motor.
items.why: Laifen went viral as a lower-priced alternative to Dyson’s Supersonic, with endless comparison videos.
items.note: Buy from the brand’s official store or authorised sellers; look-alikes are common on marketplaces.

img.alt: A woman holding a hair dryer

items.name: Under-desk walking pad
items.blurb: A slim, folding treadmill for walking while you work or watch TV.
items.why: “Walking pad era” and #deskwalking videos made them a work-from-home staple.
items.note: Built for walking, not running. Check the weight limit, and think about noise if you have neighbours below.

img.alt: A woman on a treadmill

items.name: reMarkable Paper Pro
items.blurb: A paper-like E Ink tablet for handwriting notes, sketching and reading PDFs, now with a colour screen.
items.why: Productivity and study creators love it as a distraction-free notebook.
items.note: It’s expensive, and cloud sync extras need a subscription. It isn’t a general-purpose tablet.

img.alt: A notepad on top of a laptop next to a keyboard

items.name: Kobo Libra Colour
items.blurb: A colour E Ink e-reader with page-turn buttons and optional stylus notes.
items.why: BookTok’s favourite Kindle alternative, especially for library borrowing.
items.note: Many libraries lend e-books through it via OverDrive in supported regions. Colour is softer than on a phone screen.

img.alt: An e-reader switched on

items.name: Monitor light bar
items.blurb: A slim lamp that clips onto your monitor and lights the desk without glare on the screen.
items.why: A desk-setup YouTube favourite that frees up space and looks tidy.
items.note: Check it fits your monitor; very curved or thin screens can need a different clamp.

img.alt: A latte next to a white wireless keyboard and earbuds on a desk

items.name: Kids’ digital camera
items.blurb: A chunky, drop-friendly camera with big buttons and fun photo effects for young photographers.
items.why: A consistent Amazon best-seller and a popular screen-light gift.
items.note: Image quality is basic; check whether it needs a memory card, and how photos get onto a computer.

img.alt: A child holding a camera

items.name: Fire Kids tablet
items.blurb: A tablet in a kid-proof case with parental controls and a kids’ content subscription included for a period.
items.why: One of Amazon’s top-selling devices every holiday season.
items.note: The included Amazon Kids+ subscription renews at a monthly cost unless you cancel. Set up controls before gifting.

img.alt: A young child looking at a tablet

items.name: HomeView
items.blurb: Apple’s new smart home display: a touchscreen hub for the Home app, FaceTime, music and smart home controls, in tabletop and wall-mounted versions.
items.why: Announced at Apple’s 13 October 2026 “Welcome home” launch; pre-orders are open, with availability from 13 November.
items.note: Not sold in the EU at launch. The wall-mounted version needs a separately sold mount. Brand-new product: wait for full reviews.

img.alt: A white tablet-style screen

items.name: HomePod mini 2
items.blurb: Apple’s small smart speaker gets a new chip, five colours and Sound Glow lighting that pulses with your music.
items.why: Announced 13 October 2026, on sale from 30 October, and it can team up with the new Apple TV 4K for surround sound.
items.note: The upgraded Siri arrives in a later software update, not at launch. It costs more than the original HomePod mini did.

img.alt: A black Apple HomePod speaker on a table

items.name: Pixel 11
items.blurb: Google’s mainstream Pixel, known for its cameras, bright display and on-device AI features.
items.why: One of the most-reviewed phones of the season; reviewers rate it highly but question the higher price.
items.note: It costs more than the Pixel 10 did at launch, and reviewers found little reason to upgrade from last year’s model.

img.alt: A person holding a black smartphone
